instructions: Mermoz is the user's local mailbox. Threads are issues with statuses. Search and reading are instant and offline. Sending always needs the user's approval unless they enabled agent sending.

tools.description: Full-text search across all local mail (instant, offline). Supports from:, to:, subject: prefixes. Returns threads best match first.
tools.name: search_mail

tools.description: List threads (issues) filtered by status/project/account, newest first. Statuses: unread, todo, waiting, in_progress, backlog, review, done, archive, deleted. Projects are the user's Gmail labels; each thread lists its `projects` and the AI's pending `suggestion`. `suggested`: true for threads with a pending suggestion, or {status, projects} for one destination listed by column_suggestions. `conversations`: one row per conversation (Gmail threads with the same people about the same matter, as the user sees them), each with `conversation_threads`; `kind`: ["feed", "list"] for automated senders and mailing lists.

label_id.description: Gmail label id from list_labels (pass its account_id too)

tools.name: list_threads

tools.description: Read a whole thread: every message's plain-text body, recipients and attachment ids. With `conversation`, every message of the conversation it belongs to (each with its `thread_id`), plus its people, files and links.

id.description: thread id or number like M-1287

tools.name: get_thread

tools.description: Take a thread out of the conversation Mermoz grouped it into (when it is a different matter). Final: it is never grouped with them again.
tools.name: split_conversation

tools.description: Join the conversations of two or more threads into one (same people, same matter).
tools.name: merge_conversations

tools.description: Files shared in any conversation, newest first, with their attachment id (read with get_attachment) and thread.
tools.name: list_files

tools.description: Change a thread's status, priority (0 none,1 urgent,2 high,3 normal,4 low), projects (Gmail labels: add_projects/remove_projects, or projects to replace) or due date (YYYY-MM-DD, null clears). 'deleted' moves the thread to Gmail Trash.
tools.name: update_thread

tools.description: Accept the AI's pending suggestion (status, projects, priority) for threads; they count as read. Pass `ids`, or `column` (a status) to accept that column's pending suggestions — all of them, or only the group given by `to_status`/`to_projects` as listed by column_suggestions.

to_status.description: group's target status (null: groups that only add projects)

tools.name: accept_suggestions

tools.description: Turn down the AI's pending suggestion for threads: they stay where they are and are not suggested again.
tools.name: reject_suggestions

tools.description: The AI's pending suggestions in status columns, grouped by target (status + projects) with counts, and how far background sorting has got (classified of total). Nothing moves until accepted.
tools.name: column_suggestions

tools.description: Stop a whole-mailbox sort and clear every suggestion on read threads that nobody reviewed. Accepted and turned-down suggestions are kept; Unread mail keeps its own.
tools.name: stop_resort

tools.description: Get an attachment's local file path (readable offline); text attachments also return their content.
tools.name: get_attachment

tools.description: Create a draft. With thread_id it is a reply and recipients/subject default from the thread. Drafts never send by themselves. Attachments are copied into Mermoz; Gmail sends at most 25 MB of files per email.

forward_attachments.description: attachment ids from get_thread to send again (forwarding)

tools.name: create_draft

tools.description: Ask to send a draft. Unless the user enabled agent sending, the draft goes to the user's Review lane and this returns approval_required: tell the user, do not retry.
tools.name: send_draft

tools.description: Search the user's directory, built automatically from email signatures: names, titles, companies, phones, addresses, websites. Empty query lists recent contacts.
tools.name: search_contacts

tools.description: The user's Gmail labels (mailboxes) with ids, accounts and thread counts.
tools.name: list_labels

tools.description: Workflow statuses.
tools.name: list_statuses

tools.description: Projects: the user's Gmail labels. A thread can be in several.
tools.name: list_projects

tools.description: Ask the user's own AI (the one allowed for the thread's account in Mermoz) about a thread; it sees the thread, its people, status and the user's earlier mail with them, and may search the web. The conversation is kept with the thread and shown in the app. Returns the answer and proposed actions (status, project, follow_up date, draft_reply body); nothing is applied: use update_thread or create_draft to act. Without a question, returns the conversation so far.
tools.name: chat_about_thread

tools.description: Google Drive files of a thread: those linked in its messages (with access: ok, no_access or not_connected), files shared by or with its participants, and its attachments already saved to Drive. Needs the account's Drive connected in Mermoz.
tools.name: thread_drive_files

tools.description: A Google Drive file's text: Docs as Markdown, Sheets as CSV (first sheet), Slides as text, plain-text files as they are. Cached locally.
tools.name: read_drive_file

tools.description: Search the account's Google Drive by name and content; without a query, the files the user opened most recently.
tools.name: search_drive

tools.description: Save an attachment to the user's Google Drive, in Mermoz/<the thread's project> (created if missing). Returns the folder and an Open in Drive link; saving again returns the same file. Sharing files stays with the user in the app.
tools.name: save_attachment_to_drive

tools.description: The user's Feed: every open thread as a card (one thing to do), in sections now, today, week, waiting, later, ordered by deadline then urgency. Each card has a kind (reply, decision, sign, promise, event, payment, intro, waiting, cleanup, reading, other), plain-language reasons, the deadline and amount written in the mail, and the AI's words when written. Automated mail and newsletters come as batch cards listing their threads.
tools.name: feed

tools.description: Later: hide threads from the Feed until a time (Unix ms) or until new mail arrives in them. until null brings them back now.
tools.name: snooze_thread

tools.description: Plan a change to many threads from a plain-words instruction ("archive all messages past 5 months not in done"), the way the user's Ask Mermoz bar does: the user's own AI turns it into a typed plan (filters + set status / add or remove project / mark read or unread / later / delete to Trash; nothing can send, reply or forward), and Mermoz previews it: a sentence per step, how it was understood, counts per status and sample subjects. Nothing changes. Pass `plan` (the same JSON shape as a returned `plan`) instead of `sentence` to skip the AI. Show the user the summary, then call run_bulk_action.

sentence.description: what to do, in plain words

tools.name: plan_bulk_action

tools.description: Run a plan from plan_bulk_action. `confirm` must be the plan's `total` (the number of threads it changes), as a confirmation that the preview was read. Applies in batches and returns the run id for undo_bulk_action.
tools.name: run_bulk_action

tools.description: Put every thread a bulk run changed back as it was.
tools.name: undo_bulk_action

tools.description: Report friction with these tools (missing option, confusing result, slowness) so Mermoz can improve.

text.description: what went wrong or is missing

tools.name: submit_feedback
